classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught straight-angle bisection construction at an endpoint, with the initial extension explicitly supplied. Sloping and vertical orientations require the same construction.

content.prompt: Use the construction for bisecting a straight angle to construct a right angle at the endpoint $A$ of an interval $AB$. (First produce the interval $BA$ to a point $X$.) Do this first with an interval that is on a slope, and then with one that is vertical.

answer.short: A perpendicular to the sloping interval $AB$ at $A$, with construction arcs retained.
answer.worked: Extend $BA$ through $A$ to $X$. With centre $A$, draw an arc cutting the two opposite rays at $C$ and $D$. With centres $C$ and $D$ and the same radius, greater than $AC$, draw intersecting arcs at $E$. Draw $AE$. It bisects the straight angle, so $\angle EAB=90^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Authored sloping example of the endpoint perpendicular construction taught on page 18. Dashed black arcs distinguish construction marks.
spec.mathematics: AC=AD; equal-radius arcs centred at C and D intersect at E, giving AE perpendicular to AB.

answer.short: A horizontal perpendicular to the vertical interval $AB$ at $A$, with construction arcs retained.
answer.worked: Draw $AB$ vertically and extend $BA$ through $A$ to $X$. With centre $A$, draw an arc cutting the two opposite rays at $C$ and $D$. With centres $C$ and $D$ and the same radius, greater than $AC$, draw intersecting arcs at $E$. Draw $AE$. It bisects the straight angle, so $\angle EAB=90^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Authored vertical example of the endpoint perpendicular construction taught on page 18. Dashed black arcs distinguish construction marks.
spec.mathematics: AC=AD; equal-radius arcs centred at C and D intersect at E, giving horizontal AE perpendicular to vertical AB.
